name: MSAR
tagline: Multi-stream depth attention with temporal context and adaptive stream mixing.
description: Multi-Stream Attention Residuals (MSAR) is the residual architecture introduced by Qin et al. (arXiv:2610.13630). It retrieves historical representations through multiple temporal views, using learned depth attention and adaptive stream mixing to construct each sublayer input. This benchmark evaluates MSAR with four streams, causal convolution widths 4, 8 and 12, and three-layer depth blocks. Within each block, sublayer output deltas accumulate into a single state before temporal expansion. Two-phase reads combine completed sources with the evolving partial; HPre produces a single-stream input. The first attention reads the embedding directly, and the terminal MLP returns its input plus its output delta.
mechanism: Four streams from a raw block sum and independent, zero-initialized causal temporal convolutions of widths 4, 8 and 12
Per-stream softmax depth attention over the embedding, completed blocks and current partial; two-phase read with log-partition merging
Scalar-per-stream HPre, native sublayer pre-normalization, direct first attention read and terminal MLP input-plus-output readout
limitations: Single seed 42. Compare with Standard Residual, HC and Block AttnRes at the same 23-layer depth and FFN width 6144; mHC uses FFN width 6016.
